title: Turn it; volume stays the same
hook: Swapping the height and width of an ideal box changes its drawing, not its capacity.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Separate ideal container capacity from the orientation of its dimensions.

misconception: Turning a rectangular box changes its ideal internal volume.
objective: Separate ideal container capacity from the orientation of its dimensions.

claims.text: An ideal internal box measures 20cm by 10cm by 15cm. B exchanges the last two dimensions. Scaled model; ideal inner dimensions; 1000cm³/L.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Third side=15cm, A=3L and B=3L. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.

A=["/",["*",20,10,"x"],1000]; B=["/",["*",20,"x",10],1000]; x denotes Third-side. At x=15, A=3, B=3. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. recall.question: An ideal box measures 30cm × 20cm × 10cm inside (6L). What happens to its internal capacity when it is turned onto another face?
options: It grows when stood on its smallest face
It shrinks when laid on its largest face
recall.why: Capacity is the product of the same three lengths, and order does not change a product; only fit can change.
